instructions: Heat the oven to 225°F, on convection if your oven has it. Set out 2 large baking sheets.
Rinse the kale and dry it very well in a salad spinner or with a clean towel.
Strip the leaves off the thick stems and tear them into bite size pieces.
Put the kale in a large bowl, drizzle on the 1 tbsp avocado oil and sprinkle on the 1/2 tsp salt. Rub it in with your hands until every piece looks lightly glossy.
Spread the kale over the 2 baking sheets so the pieces touch as little as possible.
Bake for 15 minutes. Turn the pans around and toss the kale lightly.
Bake for 5 to 10 minutes, until the chips are crisp and only starting to turn golden at the edges. Watch them closely at the end. They burn fast.
Leave them on the pans for 5 minutes. They crisp up more as they cool.
Serve them the same day. Leftovers keep covered at room temperature for 2 to 3 days.
method_notes: Both dry the kale very well, tear it off the stems, rub it with a little oil and salt and bake it in a single layer until crisp. Minimalist Baker (the lead) bakes one large bunch at 225°F over two sheets for 20 to 25 minutes, turning the pans halfway, and keeps leftovers 2 to 3 days. Spend With Pennies bakes at 325°F for 17 to 23 minutes. This follows the lead with avocado oil and plain salt as the seasoning.
